The provisional status YES was adopted and is not changed. The held Federal Register original was read in full and its identity confirmed (number, title, date and 83 FR pages). The packet inventory was corrected: it lacked the promulgating introductory paragraph and Section 8(e), and split Section 5(a) and 5(d)(iv) mid-sentence. No clause is shown to have ended. The only later held instrument naming the order is EO 14085 of October 3, 2022 (87 FR 60541), Section 5 of which strikes and inserts words in the introductory paragraph and Sections 1, 2, 3, 4(a), 4(c), 5(a) and 6(a); under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each affected clause continues, amended, and the before and after wording is recorded in that clause. EO 14085 has no effective-date provision, so its amendments are dated to signing. Current predicate: the original_plus_bounded_search route (held original, held later instrument attached as a later event, no own-terms end, bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog read for coverage), checked through 2026-10-14. The statutory text of titles 10 and 14 is not held, and no held source revokes or supersedes the order.
savings_reason: The order has not ended, so no savings question arises from an end. Section 8(c) itself supersedes EO 4601 and EO 9260 and keeps existing regulations under them in effect, so far as consistent, until modified or revoked by the Secretaries' regulations; which of those regulations were later modified or revoked is not shown by any held source, and the status of the order does not depend on it. The bounded searches show no further residual.

research_rationale: EO 14131 (89 FR 105377, December 27, 2024; signed December 20, 2024) amends two older orders on service certificates and badges: Section 1 replaces sections 1 and 2 of EO 12793 (Presidential Service Certificate and Badge) and Section 2 replaces sections 1, 2, 4 and 6 of EO 11926 (Vice Presidential Service Badge). The provisional status YES was adopted and is not changed. The held Federal Register original was read in full and its identity confirmed (number, title, date, 89 FR pages 105377-105379); the packet inventory of 13 clauses matches the text (the recital before Section 1 is an authority statement, not a command). Each amending clause is treated as continuing because the replacement text is the current text of the parent section, which no held instrument has revoked or amended after December 20, 2024. Under the original_plus_bounded_search route (held original, no own-terms end, no held later instrument, bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog read for coverage), checked through 2026-10-14. The packet holds no text of the current parent orders or of the 10 U.S.C. notes, so the predicate rests on the original and the bounded searches.
savings_reason: The order has not ended, so no savings question arises from an end. The order contains no savings or transition clause other than the general provisions, and the bounded searches show no residual to record.
earlier_end_check: Own terms were read in full: the order has no sunset, expiry or revocation condition, and its time phrases (at least 1 year, dates after which service counts, while assigned) are eligibility conditions inside the amended text. The packet's later-events chain is empty and the held-text search for 14131, 12793 and 11926 found no later amendment or revocation, so no earlier end is shown.
scope_check: Scope is the whole order as printed at 89 FR 105377-105379: Section 1 (a)-(b), Section 2 (a)-(d) and Section 3 general provisions. It amends the parents as already amended by EO 13286 (2003) and EO 13373 (2005); those earlier orders are context, not later events. The large EO 13286 actor file named in the dossier is not in the packet; as an earlier order it cannot end EO 14131.
independent_command_check: Each of the six amending paragraphs replaces a separate section of a parent order and is judged separately; each replacement text continues as the current wording of that section. The general provisions in Section 3 are standing rules of construction and implementation.
savings_check: No savings or transition provision in the order; Section 3 only preserves existing legal authority and OMB functions and disclaims private rights.
